info.name: 12 · Data licensing
info.description:
The platform's **data-licensing** policy: the DB-backed license catalog, the admin-only platform default, user-authored license CRUD, and the override cascade that resolves an evaluation's effective license.

**Flow.** A) the catalog (`GET /licenses[/{license_id}]`) — auth-only, no permission, readable by any role; B) the platform default (`GET`/`PATCH /platform-settings`) — admin-only; C) **user-authored license CRUD** (`licenses:create|update|delete`, admin + owner) plus the curated-is-immutable and default-is-undeletable guards; D) the **cascade** — a group `data_license_id` override vs a group that inherits the platform default, then an evaluation with its own override (wins) vs one inheriting the group's.

**Auth model.** Per-request: `{{admin_token}}` for settings + fixtures, `{{owner_token}}` for the second author, `{{viewer_token}}` / `{{redteamer_token}}` for the 403s, `noauth` for the 401. Self-contained — no `00-bootstrap`, no manual token.

**Contract notes (the string-SPDX model is gone).**
- A license is addressed by its **UUID**, not its SPDX id: `GET /licenses/{license_id}`. A slug is a **422**, and folder A asserts that explicitly so the old contract cannot silently come back.
- Curated rows (the shipped CC/ODC/CDLA set) carry an `spdx_id` and `created_by_id: null`, and are **refused for everyone** on PATCH/DELETE (403) — they are reconciled from code by `make synclicenses`.
- A user-authored row has `spdx_id: null` and `is_curated: false`.
- The platform default cannot be deleted (**409**); an unknown `default_license_id` is a **400**, not a 422.
- Overrides are `data_license_id` (UUID) and the response's `effective_license` is an **object**, not a string.

**Prereq.** `make seedlocal` (for the five role logins and the synced curated catalog).

**Leftovers.** The two evaluation groups in folder D leak — groups have no DELETE; `run_suffix` keeps them unique. Everything else is torn down.

Folder **E** covers the conversation-data protection flag: the licence field, both projections, the sealed/unsealed conversation pair, and the fact that clearing the flag leaves an existing conversation's `content_protected` untouched. Each of that pair creates a scenario first — a conversation group is posted to `/scenarios/{scenario_id}/conversation-groups`, not to the evaluation.

Verified green on a live stack: 90/90 assertions (Newman).

request.description: Holds every license permission plus the `licenses:manage` break-glass.
Holds `licenses:create|update|delete` but **not** `licenses:manage` — the second author, used to prove one author cannot edit another's row.
Can read the catalog (auth-only) but holds no license or platform-settings permission.
Holds no `licenses:create` — the create 403.

item.name: 5 · Register a model (for the cascade groups)

request.description: Folder D creates evaluation groups, and a group create requires a non-empty `allowed_model_ids`. No credential is set — nothing here talks to the provider.

exec: pm.test('the curated set is synced', () => pm.expect(items.filter(i => i.is_curated).length).to.be.above(0));
pm.test('a curated row carries an spdx_id and no author', () => { pm.expect(curated.spdx_id).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(curated.created_by_id).to.eql(null); });

request.description: The picker's source. `content` is detail-only — the list stays lean. Captures a curated id.

item.name: 2 · Get one license by its UUID

request.description: **A license is addressed by UUID.** The detail projection adds the full licence text.
A well-formed id that matches no live row.

item.name: 4 · SPDX slug → 422 (the old contract is gone)

exec: pm.test('rejected as a malformed UUID, not resolved as a slug', () => pm.expect(JSON.stringify(pm.response.json())).to.include('uuid'));

request.description: `GET /licenses/{spdx_id}` was replaced with `GET /licenses/{license_id}`. This request is a **drift guard**: it pins the fact that a slug no longer resolves, so the old contract cannot quietly return.
Catalog reads are **auth-only** — no permission gate, because every role needs the picker.
Auth-only still means authenticated.

exec: pm.test('a default license is always resolved, and it is a live catalog row', () => { const id = pm.response.json().default_license_id; pm.expect(id).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('catalog_ids') || '[]')).to.include(id); });

request.description: The singleton. Reads never persist a row — until the first PATCH this is a transient instance pointing at the curated row named by `PLATFORM_DEFAULT_DATA_LICENSE`. Captures the id so folder B can restore it.
`platform_settings:read` is admin-only.
The field is **`default_license_id`** (a UUID). The old `default_license` string is rejected as `extra_forbidden`.

exec: pm.test('names the unknown id', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include('Unknown data license'));

request.description: `validate_license_ref` rejects a reference to a non-live licence as a **400** (a domain guard), not a 422 — the id is a well-formed UUID, so schema validation passes.
`platform_settings:update` is admin-only.
Leaves the platform as it was found — folder D asserts against this value.

exec: pm.test('user-authored: no spdx_id, not curated', () => { pm.expect(b.spdx_id).to.eql(null); pm.expect(b.is_curated).to.eql(false); });
pm.test('attributed to an author (compared against the owner row in step 4)', () => pm.expect(b.created_by_id).to.be.a('string'));

body.raw:
{
  "name": "House licence {{run_suffix}}",
  "version": "1.0",
  "short_description": "Internal terms for red-team transcripts.",
  "content": "Full licence text goes here.",

}

request.description: `licenses:create`. A user-authored row is distinguished from a curated one by having an author and **no** `spdx_id`.

exec: pm.test('any role can read it', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().content).to.eql('Full licence text goes here.'));

request.description: Detail is auth-only like the list — a viewer reads any licence, authored or curated.
`licenses:update`.

exec: pm.test('attributed to the owner, not to the admin who created step 1', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().created_by_id).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('lic_admin_author')));

request.description: `owner` holds `licenses:create` too — licences are not admin-only.

item.name: 5 · Admin edits the owner's licence (licenses:manage break-glass)

request.description: The admin-only `licenses:manage` break-glass reaches **another user's** licence.
Holding `licenses:update` governs your **own** rows; without `licenses:manage` another author's row is refused.
`red_teamer` holds no `licenses:create`.
Curated rows are reconciled from code by `sync_licenses`, so an API edit would be reverted on the next deploy. Refused even for an admin holding `licenses:manage`.
Same rule on the delete path.
Sets up the delete guard below.

exec: pm.test('tells the caller what to do first', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().detail).to.include('set another default'));

request.description: A licence every unset group/evaluation resolves to cannot be removed while it holds that role.

item.name: 12 · Restore the default, then delete ours

request.description: Releases the guard so the teardown can proceed.
Soft delete. Groups/evaluations that already reference a tombstoned licence keep resolving it.
Via the same `licenses:manage` break-glass as step 5.

exec: pm.test('raw override is the id we set', () => pm.expect(b.data_license_id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('curated_id')));

pm.test('effective_license is an OBJECT resolving to it', () => { pm.expect(b.effective_license).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(b.effective_license.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('curated_id')); });

request.description: `data_license_id` is the raw override; `effective_license` is the **resolved object** (`{id, spdx_id, name, ...}`). Both used to be SPDX strings.

item.name: 2 · Approve it (evaluations need an approved group)

request.description: A fresh group is `pending_approval` and evaluation creation 409s until it is approved; an owner may self-approve.
With nothing set at the group level the cascade falls through to the platform default.
Same precondition as step 2.

exec: pm.test('evaluation override beats the inherited default', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().effective_license.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('curated_id')));

request.description: Most-specific wins: Platform default → Group override → **Evaluation override**. Deliberately placed in the *inheriting* group so the override is the only thing that can explain the result.
An omitted `data_license_id` means *inherit*, never *reset to none*.

item.name: E · Conversation-data protection
1 · Create a licence that protects conversation data

request.description: A user-authored licence may declare that it protects the conversations written under it: message text in a conversation created under it is stored **encrypted at rest**. Titles, tags and attachments are not covered.

item.name: 2 · Read it back — the flag is on the detail projection

request.description: `DataLicenseResponse` projects the flag, so a client can tell whether choosing this licence will seal transcripts.

exec: pm.test('summary carries the flag too', () => { pm.expect(row).to.be.an('object'); pm.expect(row.protects_conversation_data).to.eql(true); });

request.description: `DataLicenseSummary` carries it as well — the licence picker marks the option without a second round-trip.
The conversation inherits its protection from the evaluation's **effective** licence, so the cascade is what decides sealing — not a per-conversation switch.
A conversation runs against an **assignment**, not a bare model — the body is `{model_id}` and the response id is the `evaluation_ai_model_id` the conversation needs.
A conversation lives under a scenario, so the evaluation needs one before the group below.

item.name: 7 · A conversation started here is sealed

request.description: `ConversationResponse.content_protected` is resolved **once, at creation**, from the evaluation's effective licence. From here every message written into this conversation is stored as ciphertext and served as plaintext.

item.name: 8 · An evaluation inheriting the platform default

exec: pm.test('the inherited licence does NOT protect', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().effective_license.protects_conversation_data).to.eql(false));

request.description: The control half of the pair. Asserting the inherited licence's flag here rather than assuming it means that if the platform default ever becomes a protecting licence, this step fails loudly instead of the next one flipping silently.

item.name: 9 · Assign the model to it as well
10 · Create a scenario for it as well

request.description: A conversation lives under a scenario, so the evaluation needs one before the group below.
Same request shape, different licence — so the only thing that can explain the difference is the licence flag.

item.name: 12 · Clearing the flag on the licence

request.description: The author (or a `licenses:manage` holder) may turn the flag off. What that does **not** do is the point of the next step.

item.name: 13 · …does not reach a conversation already created

request.description: The decision is frozen at creation and never re-derived, so `content_protected` can legitimately disagree with the licence's current flag. Rows already sealed stay sealed — clearing the flag only changes what happens to conversations started from now on.

item.name: 14 · A curated licence refuses the flag

request.description: Curated rows are code-owned: `content` is the single field the API accepts on them, and only where the catalog ships none. Every other field — this one included — is refused for everyone, because the next `synclicenses` would revert it.

item.description:
The licence flag that decides whether message text is **encrypted at rest**, and the per-conversation field that reports the decision.

The pair of conversation creates — one sealed, one not — is the load-bearing part: two conversations started by the same request shape, each under its own scenario, differing only in the licence their evaluation resolves to. The re-read after the licence flag is cleared pins the promise the contract makes — that `content_protected` is taken once at creation and can therefore disagree with the licence's current flag.

Sealing covers `messages.content` only; conversation titles, tags and attachments stay in the clear, and an export unseals the text by design.

request.description: Children before parents.
The second cascade fixture. Both evaluations go before the model, whose assignment they would otherwise still reference.
The two evaluation groups leak — groups have no DELETE route; `run_suffix` keeps their titles unique.
